policy_sources.title: Invoice Exception Handling
policy_sources.excerpt:
# Invoice Exception Handling

When invoice data does not agree with an approved purchase order, receipt, or
invoice arithmetic, do not treat the automated match as approval to pay. Compare
the cited invoice and purchase-order evidence, confirm the applicable contract
or approved change, and request a corrected invoice or documented approval when
the source documents disagree. Keep the issue open until a finance reviewer
records a decision.

For unit-price differences, compare the invoice unit price with the approved
purchase-order unit price. For line-total and grand-total differences, recalculate
the arithmetic from the cited quantities, prices, taxable value, and tax lines.
Do not substitute an estimated amount for a missing source value.

For tax type, rate, or amount differences, confirm the supplier and buyer tax
jurisdictions and compare invoice tax components with the purchase-ord

policy_sources.title: Payment and Duplicate Review
policy_sources.excerpt:
# Payment and Duplicate Review

An invoice marked as a possible duplicate or a bank debit that differs from an
invoice total must be reviewed before further payment processing. Compare the
referenced invoice, bank statement, remittance advice, and prior payment ledger.
Determine whether the difference is a partial payment, approved deduction,
duplicate debit, or an unresolved discrepancy; record the supporting evidence
and route unresolved items to a finance reviewer.

Automated matching and anomaly findings are review signals only. They do not
authorize, initiate, or release a payment. Never send a vendor communication
automatically; prepare correspondence as a draft for human review.
